chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who married a woman, and she said to him, "I am pregnant," or "I am your sister through breastfeeding," or "I am not free of a waiting period ('iddah)." He said: "If he has entered upon her and had intercourse with her, then he should not believe her. But if he has not entered upon her and has not had intercourse with her, then he should act with precaution and inquire, if he did not know her before that."

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: consummated the marriage by entering upon her
key_terms.عِدَّةٍ: the waiting period after separation or widowhood
key_terms.فَلْيَحْتَطْ: let him act cautiously and take precaution

ai.seo_question: What should a man do if his wife claims after marriage that she is pregnant, his foster sister, or still in 'iddah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a woman making a claim after marriage that would invalidate or complicate the union, such as pregnancy, foster-kinship, or being in 'iddah. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام distinguishes between a marriage already consummated and one not yet consummated, instructing precaution and investigation before consummation when the husband lacked prior knowledge.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4640 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Basir who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about a man who married a woman, and she told him, "I am pregnant," or "I am your sister through breastfeeding," or "I am still in my waiting period (iddah)."
Imam (as) said: "If he has already been intimate with her and consummated the marriage, he should not believe her. But if he has not been intimate with her and has not consummated the marriage, then he should take precaution and inquire if he was not aware of her situation beforehand."
